questions.concept: Maxterm formation for an input combination
questions.question: In canonical POS form, which maxterm corresponds to the input combination A = 1, B = 0, C = 1?
questions.explanation: A maxterm is an OR term for a row where the output is 0. In a maxterm a variable equal to 0 is written uncomplemented and a variable equal to 1 is complemented, giving A' + B + C'.

questions.question: Which statement about the halting problem is correct?

options.A: A sufficiently powerful Turing machine can always decide it
options.B: Alonzo Church proved it decidable using lambda calculus
options.C: Linear bounded automata can decide it but pushdown automata cannot
options.D: Turing proved in 1936 that it is undecidable for Turing machines

questions.explanation: The halting problem asks whether a program will finish or run forever. In 1936 Alan Turing proved it undecidable: no Turing machine can decide it correctly for all program/input pairs.

questions.concept: sorted() on a tuple returns a new list
questions.question: What does sorted(("Rama", "Heena", "Raj")) return in Python?
questions.explanation: sorted() takes the elements of a sequence and returns a new sorted list, even when the input is a tuple. The strings are arranged alphabetically, so the result is a list.

questions.question: In an ER diagram, a weak entity is represented by which symbol?
questions.explanation: A weak entity cannot be uniquely identified by its own attributes and is drawn as a double rectangle. A dashed oval marks a derived attribute and double ellipses a multivalued attribute.

questions.question: How many cables are required to connect 6 computers in a fully connected mesh topology?
questions.explanation: A fully connected mesh with n nodes needs n(n-1)/2 wires: 6 x 5 / 2 = 15.

questions.concept: Validation checks that the right product is built
questions.question: Which activity checks whether the right product has been built for the user's needs and is the responsibility of all stakeholders?
questions.explanation: Validation checks whether the right product was built for user needs and involves all stakeholders. Verification checks whether the product was built correctly.

questions.question: Card data is secretly copied by a device while a customer makes a legitimate debit card transaction. This attack is called:
questions.explanation: Skimming copies credit or debit card data during legitimate transactions. Smishing uses SMS, sniffing captures network packets and spoofing fakes IP or DNS identity.

questions.concept: Encoder made up of OR gates
questions.question: An encoder, a device that converts analog signals into digital signals, is made up of which logic gates?
questions.explanation: As per the syllabus, an encoder is made up of OR gates. XOR gates are associated with the half adder instead.

questions.question: Which open, global, packet-based IoT protocol, based on IEEE 802.15.4, is used by smart bulbs, smart locks and door sensors?
questions.explanation: Zigbee (IEEE 802.15.4) is an open, global, packet-based protocol for low-cost, low-power communication in a PAN. Smart bulbs, plugs, locks and sensors use it.

questions.question: In process state transitions, a process moves from the Running state back to the Ready state because of:
questions.explanation: Running to Ready happens on an interrupt. An I/O or event wait moves Running to Wait/Block, dispatch moves Ready to Running and exit moves Running to Terminated.

questions.question: Which protocol controls media sessions between client and server, enabling play, pause and fast-forward as on Netflix?
questions.explanation: RTSP (Real-Time Streaming Protocol) controls media sessions such as play, pause and fast forward. RTP is used for video conferencing and live streaming.

questions.concept: Prim's algorithm starts from any vertex
questions.question: Which minimum spanning tree algorithm starts with any vertex and repeatedly chooses the minimum weight edge from the already connected vertices?
questions.explanation: Prim's algorithm is greedy, starts with any vertex and picks the minimum weight edge from connected vertices. Kruskal's algorithm instead starts with the least weighted edge in the whole graph.
Array indexing starts at 0, so a[3] is 8. Multiplication has higher precedence than addition, so 8 + 6 = 14.

questions.concept: Language class of Linear Bounded Automata
questions.question: In the Chomsky hierarchy, which language class is exactly characterized by Linear Bounded Automata?
questions.explanation: Type 1 context-sensitive languages are accepted by Linear Bounded Automata. Type 0 maps to Turing machines, Type 2 to pushdown automata and Type 3 to finite automata.

questions.question: The pattern used to identify a particular computer virus is called a:
questions.explanation: A virus signature is the pattern used to identify a virus, and antivirus software matches files against such signatures.

questions.question: According to the Python version history, how many keywords did Python 3.0 (2008) have?
questions.explanation: Python 2.0 (2000) had 30 keywords, Python 3.0 (2008) had 33 and Python 3.8 (2019) has 35.

questions.question: An attribute 'Address' that is made up of pin code, state and country is an example of which attribute type?
questions.explanation: A composite attribute is a combination of other attributes, such as an address composed of pin code, state and country.

questions.question: When the waiting queue is full and RAM is limited, a process is swapped out to secondary memory and enters the Suspend state. Which scheduler handles this swap?
questions.explanation: The medium-term scheduler performs swap-in and swap-out between RAM and secondary memory, which is how processes enter the Suspend state.

questions.question: Which technology superimposes computer-generated information over the existing physical surroundings instead of creating a completely new environment?
questions.explanation: Augmented Reality overlays digital information on the real world. Unlike Virtual Reality, it does not create a new simulated environment.

questions.question: Based on De Morgan's theorem (A + B)' = A'.B', a NOR gate is equivalent to which gate?
questions.explanation: (A + B)' = A'.B' means a NOR gate equals an AND gate with inverted (bubbled) inputs. By the other law (A.B)' = A' + B', a NAND gate is a bubbled OR.

questions.question: Which type of testing checks that a new version of software still works with files and environments of its older version?
questions.explanation: Backward compatibility testing checks that a new version works with older version files and environments. Browser compatibility testing instead checks different browser and OS combinations.

questions.question: Which year-event pairing from the evolution of networking timeline is correct?
questions.explanation: DNS was introduced in 1983. ARPANET became functional in 1969, e-mail came in 1971, TCP/IP became the ARPANET standard in 1982 and NSFNET expanded in 1986.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of lossless compression?
questions.explanation: Lossless compression keeps all original quality; examples include ZIP, PNG, BMP, WAV, FLAC, GIF and PDF. JPEG, MP3 and MPEG are lossy.

questions.question: Which C++ storage class has global visibility?
questions.explanation: The extern storage class gives a variable global visibility across files; auto and register are local to their block.

questions.question: A binary tree in which every node has either 0 or 2 children is called a:
questions.explanation: A full, proper or strict binary tree has every node with 0 or 2 children. A complete tree fills all levels except possibly the last; a perfect tree fills all levels.
